# Proposal: Guided AI GRC Build for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel (Sponsor and stated budget holder)
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, twelve weeks, US$60,000
**Basis:** Client Profile Block v1.0 and discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. The Client has about 1,100 staff, is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. Revenue was described as "in the US$200 to 300 million range." This figure was given verbally and has not been checked against filings.

The Client's AI portfolio is at an early stage and has three components:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

Several pressures shape the work:

- **Internal audit finding (June 2026):** no inventory of AI systems exists.
- **Regulatory drivers:** the EU AI Act and GDPR.
- **Certification interest:** ISO/IEC 42001 work is expected to start next year, but no start date has been fixed.
- **Existing management systems:** the Client runs an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and an ISO 9001 quality management system.

Your stated objective is clear: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Three constraints apply:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Consulting Delivery

A conventional consulting engagement would hand Tamarack a finished set of documents. That approach leaves the knowledge with the consultant and the operating burden with a team that did not build the system.

The Guided AI GRC Build works the other way. Your own team builds the AI Management System (AIMS) week by week, with structured workshops, coaching and asynchronous implementation between sessions. At Week 12 the people who will run the system are the people who wrote it. They understand why each control exists and can operate, defend and improve it without outside dependence.

This matters for three reasons:

- **The audit finding needs a sustained fix.** It calls for an inventory that is maintained, not a one-time snapshot.
- **ISO/IEC 42001 rewards a working system.** Readiness depends on operating evidence rather than documents alone.
- **The works council consultation needs internal ownership.** It requires internal ownership and judgment that cannot be outsourced.

The program rests on three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

It draws on three public framework repositories:

- **GRC Workbook:** https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook
- **Slow AI Kitchen:** https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen
- **AI Governance for Boards (board-layer reference):** https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack

**Inventory priority (Weeks 2 to 5).** The three named systems enter the inventory first, in this order:

1. **Customer service chatbot.** It is the only deployed system and the one in live customer contact. It is therefore the most immediate GDPR and EU data residency question.
2. **Visual inspection pilot.** It is the system your Q2 2027 objective is built around, and the one that triggers works council consultation.
3. **Sales forecasting.** It enters as a planned system so that governance is in place before procurement or build begins.

Any further AI use across the business is Unknown until the Week 2 discovery sweep.

**ISO/IEC 42001 mapping.** Each week's artifacts are mapped to ISO/IEC 42001 readiness themes. This is readiness preparation only. It is not a promise of certification or any audit outcome.

**Integration with existing management systems.** The intent is to integrate with the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and ISO 9001 QMS rather than build parallel structures. The Profile Block does not identify which ISMS or QMS registers, processes or records already exist. Every integration point is therefore marked Unknown in the table below until Week 1 confirms the specific artifacts.

| Week | Focus, tailored to Tamarack | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme | Integration point |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Mobilization, AIMS charter and roles; confirm build team, steering attendees and second workflow candidate | Context, leadership, roles | Unknown |
| W2 | AI system inventory: chatbot, visual inspection pilot, sales forecasting, then discovery sweep; record data location for each system (currently Unknown) | AIMS scope | Unknown |
| W3 | Classification and risk methodology, including EU AI Act classification of each system (confirm with external counsel) | Risk criteria | Unknown |
| W4 | Risk and impact assessments for chatbot and visual inspection; GDPR and works council considerations captured (confirm with external counsel) | AI risk assessment, AI system impact assessment | Unknown |
| W5 | Risk register and treatment plans | Risk treatment, control selection | Unknown |

| W12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Internal audit and management review preparedness | Unknown |

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome is a minimum viable AIMS consisting of six elements:

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

**Scoping decision required: the second governed workflow.** The chatbot is the only system the Profile Block describes as deployed. The visual inspection system is in pilot and is targeted for production in Q2 2027.

The program start date is Unknown, so Week 12 timing is also Unknown. If the program started in early January 2027, Week 12 would fall in late March 2027. In that case visual inspection would count as the second workflow only if it entered production use within the program window. That would require works council consultation to be completed first.

The alternative is another AI workflow already in production use, which is Unknown today. We ask you to decide at Week 1 which route applies so the contracted outcome is achievable on the facts. Any decision touching production staff carries this note: confirm with external counsel.

Two points are worth flagging now:

- **Auditor independence.** Internal auditors who help build the AIMS may later face independence questions when auditing it. We recommend agreeing their role boundaries at Week 1.
- **Unconfirmed ownership.** Ownership of each AI system is not stated in the Profile Block and is recorded as Unknown until Week 1 confirms it.

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints take place at Weeks 1, 6 and 12:

- **Week 1:** confirms scope, team, delivery risks and the second workflow decision.
- **Week 6:** reviews spine status, blockers and any scope adjustments.
- **Week 12:** reviews the minimum viable AIMS against the six elements and approves the 12-month operating plan.

Steering attendees beyond the Sponsor are Unknown and will be confirmed at mobilization.
